etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin minimus +‎ -ize.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To make (something) smaller or as small as possible; shrink; reduce.

quote.citation: 1948, Willard Price, Roving South, Rio Grande to Patagonia, New York, N.Y.: J. Day Co., →OCLC, page 13:
quote.text: Terry, author of the indispensable Terry's Guide to Mexico, has a name for it – atrabiliousness. "The defect of many of the murals," he says, speaking of those in the orphan asylum, "is the facial atrabiliousness of some of the subjects. To the observer it minimizes the grandeur of the conception  […] "

quote.citation: 1954, Instruments and Control Systems - Volume 27, page 1466:
quote.text: For accurate stopping, the drive must incorporate means for minimizing inertia overdrift.
One way to minimize or mitigate the copycat effect is to deemphasize the perpetrator and deglorify the violence in real and fictional stories.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To relegate or assign (something) to a less insignificant status; diminish.
(computing, transitive, graphical user interface) To remove (a window) from the main display area, collapsing it to an icon or caption.
(transitive) To treat (someone) in a slighting manner.

quote.citation: 1993, Jan McDaniel, One Golden Summer, page 95:
quote.text: […]  father who had never openly minimized him or anything he did  […]
